rows.basis: Q3 2023 release says Tesla more than doubled its AI training compute for its dataset and Optimus; no AI capex amount is stated against FY2023 capex of $8.899B.

Q1 2024 release states AI infrastructure capex of $1.0B in Q1 only; $1.0B ÷ FY2024 capex $11.342B. This is a lower bound: Q2 release separately states $0.6B (H1 $1.6B), and no AI amount is stated for H2 or the full year.

10-K says FY2025 capex of $8.53B was mainly for global AI and operational infrastructure and factory expansion; releases cite 16k H200 GPUs added (Cortex at 67k H100 equivalents) and Cortex 2 under construction. No AI amount stated.
Q1 2024 release says Tesla will continue to increase core AI infrastructure capacity; the 10-K guide of over $11B for 2025 is a company total with no AI part.

FY2025 10-K guides 2026 capex in excess of $20B, driven by AI initiatives (compute infrastructure, data centers) among other uses; this is the company total, not the AI part. Release plans to more than double Texas onsite compute in H1 2026. No AI amount; later guidance changes are not broken out by program.
Releases and 10-K attribute the opex increase partly to Cybertruck, AI and other R&D programs; no AI amount is stated against FY2023 opex of $8.769B.
10-K says the opex increases were primarily driven by AI program costs; releases say the same quarterly. No AI amount is stated against FY2024 opex of $10.374B.
10-K says R&D rose $1.87B (41%), mainly from AI and other programs plus $500M more SBC; releases cite AI and other R&D projects. The AI part is not separated from the $12.739B opex.
Q3 2026 release says rising data center demand should keep driving demand for Tesla's products (energy storage context). This is words only, with no AI or data-center revenue amount or share.
